title: Social cohesion in co-located, remote and hybrid teams
blurb: Explain social cohesion, why dispersed teams must build it deliberately, and who looks after the team's cohesion, safety and well-being.
question: A project team is split across three cities and home workers, and testers and developers barely trust each other. What does PRINCE2 suggest?

teach.body: When PRINCE2 7 talks about bringing teams together, it means making good use of people's time and building social cohesion. Social cohesion develops when people meet in a purposeful way on a regular basis, building trust across project silos. In plain English: a team that only meets to report status is a group of silos; a team that regularly works through real problems together starts to trust each other.

teach.h: Co-located versus virtual, remote or hybrid
teach.caption: How teams communicate also depends on whether they are co-located, remote or hybrid (manual 3.4).

teach.body: In a co-located team, information tends to flow organically through formal and informal networks. When teams are virtual, distant from each other or hybrid, that does not happen by itself, so social cohesion has to be considered more deliberately. PRINCE2's example is syncing co-location days for key people or teams, with a focus on building key relationships.

steps.label:
Sync co-location
days
steps.sub: for the key people or teams

teach.body: Cohesion also rests on ways of working people accept. Team building aims to build trust and find compatible ways of working, and co-creating those ways of working makes people more willing to follow them. In practice, that means agreeing norms together (when to be online, how decisions are recorded) and running meetings that work equally well for people in the room and people dialling in.

teach.h: Who looks after cohesion and well-being
head: Role or point
Responsibility
rows: Supports social cohesion; focuses on team safety and well-being
Monitors and supports team members' safety and well-being
Monitors and supports their team's safety and well-being
Team performance, health and well-being reviewed
teach.caption: From the PRINCE2 7 role descriptions and the organizing practice in 'managing a stage boundary' and 'closing a project'.

teach.h: How is the team set up?

children.label: Plan cohesion deliberately
children.sub: for example co-location days for key people

teach.h: Worked scenario: Marlow Vale Building Society
teach.body: Marlow Vale is replacing its mortgage system. Developers work in Leeds, analysts mostly from home and testers at a supplier in Cardiff. Project manager Rachel Kim notices testers and developers blaming each other in tickets. She arranges a monthly co-location day for the leads, a fortnightly joint session to work through defects together, and co-creates team norms on response times. Executive Paul Dunn asks at each stage boundary how the late-night releases are affecting people's well-being.

teach.text: Social cohesion is not the same as more status meetings. Collecting progress updates belongs to the progress practice; cohesion comes from people meeting purposefully and regularly to build trust across silos. And do not assume a dispersed team will share information organically as a co-located one does.

items: Bringing teams together means optimizing people's time and building social cohesion (manual 3.3.3).
Social cohesion: people meeting purposefully and regularly, building trust across project silos.
Co-located teams share information organically; virtual, remote and hybrid teams need deliberate methods such as synchronized co-location days for key people.
The board supports social cohesion and focuses on the team's safety and well-being; the PM and team managers monitor and support well-being.
Team performance, health and well-being are reviewed at stage boundaries and at closure.

summary: You can now explain social cohesion as trust built through purposeful, regular contact, and why virtual, remote and hybrid teams need deliberate methods to build it. You can also say who looks after the team's cohesion, safety and well-being.

A.q: How does PRINCE2 say social cohesion is developed?
options: Through formal reporting at the end of each stage
People meeting purposefully and regularly, building trust
By assigning every team member to a single team manager for the project
Through the change authority approving team changes
A.why: Social cohesion is developed by people meeting in a purposeful way on a regular basis, building trust across project silos (manual 3.3.3).

whyNot.0: End stage reporting is a progress control, not how cohesion is built.
whyNot.2: Reporting lines do not create trust across silos.
whyNot.3: The change authority deals with requests for change to baselines, not team cohesion.

A.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. In a [?] team, information tends to be shared organically through formal and informal networks.
options: virtual
hybrid
geographically remote
co-located
A.why: PRINCE2 notes that co-located teams tend to share information organically (manual 3.3.3).

whyNot.0: Virtual teams need social cohesion to be built more deliberately.
whyNot.1: Hybrid teams need deliberate methods because information does not flow as organically.
whyNot.2: Remote teams, located at a distance, need deliberate methods to build cohesion.

A.q: Which method does PRINCE2 give as an example for building social cohesion in a hybrid team?
options: Synchronized co-location days for key people
More frequent highlight reports to the board
Moving all communication to written reports
Splitting the project into more stages
A.why: Syncing co-location days for key people or teams, focusing on key relationships, is the example PRINCE2 gives (manual 3.3.3).

whyNot.1: Highlight reports keep the board informed of stage status; they do not build trust within the team.
whyNot.2: Written reports reduce contact and do little to build trust across silos.
whyNot.3: Stages are decision and control points, not a way of building cohesion.

B.q:
Which two statements about social cohesion are correct?
1. Virtual and hybrid teams need social cohesion to be considered more deliberately.
2. Social cohesion is mainly built through formal reporting at stage ends.
3. Bringing teams together should make good use of people's time.
4. Supporting social cohesion is outside the project board's role.
options: 1 and 2
2 and 4
1 and 3
3 and 4
B.why: Dispersed teams need cohesion built deliberately (1), and bringing teams together should optimize people's time as well as build cohesion (3) (manual 3.3.3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: cohesion comes from purposeful, regular meetings that build trust.
whyNot.1: Both are false: formal reporting does not build cohesion, and the board's role includes supporting it.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: the board's role description includes monitoring and supporting social cohesion.

B.q: A project team works across three cities and a home-based group. Testers and developers rarely interact and trust between them is low. What should the project manager do?
options: Plan regular, purposeful contact such as co-location days for key people
Increase checkpoint report frequency to monitor the testers more closely
Ask the board to raise stage tolerances to absorb the friction
Let informal networks share information over the coming months
B.why: Dispersed teams need social cohesion built deliberately, for example through synchronized co-location days and purposeful, regular meetings (manual 3.3.3).

whyNot.1: More reporting monitors work but does not build trust across silos.
whyNot.2: Tolerances deal with performance variation, not the relationship problem.
whyNot.3: Informal networks work organically in co-located teams; dispersed teams need deliberate methods.

B.q: Which role's description includes monitoring and supporting social cohesion within the project ecosystem?
options: Project support
Team manager
Project assurance
Project board
B.why: The project board's responsibilities include monitoring and supporting social cohesion within the project ecosystem.

whyNot.0: Project support provides administrative services such as registers and meeting support.
whyNot.1: The team manager manages relationships in the team and supports their well-being, but this responsibility is listed for the board.
whyNot.2: Project assurance checks the project's performance and products independently of the PM.

C.q: A project manager arranges a fortnightly in-person day for a hybrid team's key people to work through shared problems together. A team manager suggests turning it into a progress meeting instead. Which statement reflects PRINCE2 guidance?
options: A progress meeting fits best, as it saves reporting effort
Its purpose is to build social cohesion and trust across silos
It should stop, as some people cannot attend in person each time
It should be replaced by one team-building event at the start
C.why: Purposeful, regular contact builds social cohesion and trust across project silos, which hybrid teams need deliberately (manual 3.3.3).

whyNot.0: Progress is reported through checkpoint and highlight reports; turning the day into status reporting loses its cohesion purpose.
whyNot.2: Not everyone attending each time does not remove the value of regular purposeful contact.
whyNot.3: Team building can accelerate formation, but cohesion relies on regular contact throughout.

C.q: Which pairing of a role and a people responsibility is correct?
options: Project support: safety and well-being of the whole team
Project assurance: social cohesion across the ecosystem
Team manager: safety and well-being of team members
Business layer: day-to-day well-being of the team
C.why: The team manager's role description includes monitoring and supporting the safety and well-being of team members.

whyNot.0: Project support provides administrative services; well-being sits with the board, PM and team managers.
whyNot.1: Supporting social cohesion is in the project board's role description, not assurance's.
whyNot.3: The business layer sits outside the project and does not manage the team day to day.

C.q: When does PRINCE2 review project team performance, health and well-being, and why?
options: At stage boundaries and closure, to inform reports and lessons
At each checkpoint, to set the next work package's tolerances
In starting up a project, to appoint the executive
After closure, as part of post-project benefits reviews
C.why: In 'managing a stage boundary' and 'closing a project', team performance, health and well-being are reviewed for lessons and for the end stage or end project report.

whyNot.1: Checkpoints report work package progress; tolerances are set when the work package is authorized.
whyNot.2: Appointing the executive happens in starting up a project and is not a team well-being review.
whyNot.3: Post-project benefits reviews check benefits after closure, not team well-being.

reteach.title: The online choir
reteach.question: Why does an online choir sound worse than one that rehearses in the same hall?

blocks.body: Singers in one hall pick up each other's timing and mood without trying. Spread across kitchens on video, they lose that, so the director has to plan it: regular sessions with a clear purpose, an occasional weekend together for the section leaders, and norms everyone agreed. And someone keeps an eye on whether people are coping, not just whether they hit the notes.

blocks.text: A weekly roll call of who practised is not harmony. Status checks are progress; cohesion is purposeful contact that builds trust.

explain.body: Social cohesion develops when people meet purposefully and regularly, building trust across project silos.

test.q: What builds social cohesion, according to PRINCE2?
options: Detailed role descriptions
Tighter time tolerances
More formal reporting
Purposeful, regular meetings
test.why: Social cohesion is developed by people meeting purposefully and regularly (manual 3.3.3).

whyNot.0: Role descriptions clarify responsibilities but do not by themselves build trust.
whyNot.1: Tolerances are controls for manage by exception.
whyNot.2: Formal reports serve the progress practice, not cohesion.

explain.body: In co-located teams, information tends to be shared organically through formal and informal networks.

test.q: Which type of team tends to share information organically through informal networks?
options: Virtual
Geographically remote
Co-located
Hybrid
test.why: Co-located teams tend to share information organically (manual 3.3.3).

whyNot.0: Virtual teams need cohesion built deliberately.
whyNot.1: Remote teams are at a distance and need deliberate methods.
whyNot.3: Hybrid teams need deliberate methods for the people not together.

explain.body: When teams are virtual, distant or hybrid, building social cohesion must be considered more deliberately, for example by syncing co-location days for key people or teams.

test.q: Why do dispersed teams need deliberate methods to build cohesion?
options: Virtual teams are exempt from the regular progress reporting
Information does not flow as it does when co-located
The board must approve each remote meeting held
Trust matters less when people work remotely
test.why: Without the organic sharing of a co-located team, cohesion has to be built on purpose (manual 3.3.3).

whyNot.0: Reporting arrangements still apply to virtual teams.
whyNot.2: The board does not approve individual team meetings.
whyNot.3: Trust matters just as much; it is simply harder to build at a distance.

explain.body: In PRINCE2 7 the project board focuses on the safety and well-being of the project team and supports social cohesion; the project manager and team managers monitor and support team members' well-being.

test.q: At directing level, which part of the project management team focuses on the safety and well-being of the project team?
options: Business layer
Project support
Project board
Project assurance
test.why: The project board's responsibilities include focusing on the safety and well-being of the project team.

whyNot.0: The business layer is outside the project management team.
whyNot.1: Project support works at the managing level providing administrative services.
whyNot.3: Project assurance checks the project independently of the PM; it is not the directing body.
